mainTopic: Gifts of a sick person: a partial gift (מתנת שכיב מרע במקצת) versus a gift given because of expected death (מצוה מחמת מיתה)
overview: The גמרא finishes a story about a sick woman who kept giving her property to רב דימי and taking it back whenever she recovered. Once, רב דימי left part of the property for her and made a קנין on the rest, but she still took it back when she got better. רב נחמן asked the witnesses what she had said. She had cried out that she was dying, so he ruled that she was a מצוה מחמת מיתה and could retract. The גמרא then asks about a שכיב מרע who gives away only part of his property. The רבנן quoted רב נחמן as saying such a gift needs no קנין, but רבא rejects that version and says it needs a קנין, like a healthy person's gift. רבא defends this against challenges from a משנה, from the story of the mother of בני רוכל, and from a משנה in גיטין. He explains that the sources without a קנין are cases of a מצוה מחמת מיתה. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע offers a different explanation. The final הלכה: a partial gift needs a קנין, while a מצוה מחמת מיתה needs none if he dies and can be retracted if he recovers, even after a קנין.

steps.title: The woman's habit and her offer to רב דימי
steps.stepSummary: Whenever the woman recovered, she would take back her gift. Once, when she was sick, she told רב דימי to come and acquire the property in any way he wanted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when she recovered, she would take it back. One time she got sick. She sent him a message: 'Come and acquire.' He sent back: 'I don't want to.' She sent him another message: 'Come and acquire in any way you want.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues a story. It describes the woman's habit of retracting and sets up the episode in which רב דימי tries to make the gift final.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A gift given by a שכיב מרע can normally be taken back if the giver recovers. רב דימי refused at first, probably tired of gifts that keep getting taken back. When she offered 'any way you want,' it opened the door for him to do something that would make the gift stick.

keyTerms.meaning: She stood up, meaning she recovered from her illness
She retracted, took back her gift

phrases.english: And when she recovered, she would retract it.
One time she became sick,
she sent him a message: Come, acquire.
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רב דימי, the man she kept giving the property to.

phrases.english: He sent back: I do not want to.
She sent him a message: Come, acquire
in any way that you want.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a story that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Background: the woman's gifts were normally retracted when she recovered.

steps.title: רב דימי leaves part for her and makes a קנין, but she retracts anyway
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי left some of the property for her and made a formal קנין on the rest. When she recovered, she took it back again.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went, left over a part for her, and acquired the rest from her with a קנין. When she recovered, she took it back.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי does two things meant to make the gift final, but the woman still retracts after she recovers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving over part of the property makes it a partial gift, and a partial gift is treated like a healthy person's gift that cannot be taken back. Making a קנין also normally makes a gift final. So רב דימי thought he had closed every loophole.

keyTerms.meaning: He left over, reserved a portion
They made a קנין from her, a formal act of acquisition

phrases.english: He went and left over a part for her
and acquired the rest from her with a קנין.
When she recovered, she retracted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows what רב דימי did with her offer and how she responded.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The disputed case: a partial gift with a קנין, followed by a retraction after she recovered.

steps.title: רב דימי refuses to come to court
steps.stepSummary: The woman brought her case to רב נחמן, who summoned רב דימי. רב דימי refused to come, arguing that the leftover portion and the קנין made the gift final.
steps.simpleTranslation: She came before רב נחמן. He sent for רב דימי: 'Come.' He did not come. He said: 'Why should I come? I left over a part for her and acquired from her!'
steps.whatsHappening: The case goes to court, and רב דימי gives his legal reason why there is nothing to argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב דימי's claim rests on two points: the gift was partial, and a קנין was made. Either one should normally stop a retraction. He thinks the case is closed before it starts.

keyTerms.meaning: Before him, meaning in front of a judge

phrases.english: She came before Rav Nachman,
he sent him a message: Come.
He did not come.
He said: Why should I come?
I left over a part for her and acquired from her!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the story into a court case and gives רב דימי's position.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב דימי's claim: a partial gift with a קנין cannot be retracted.

steps.title: רב נחמן threatens נידוי
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן warned רב דימי that if he did not come, he would be put in נידוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent him: 'If you don't come, I will strike you with a thorn that does not draw blood.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן insists that רב דימי appear in court and threatens a punishment if he does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 'thorn that does not draw blood' is a picture of נידוי: it hurts without leaving a wound. The point is that no one can decide on his own that a case is over. The court must hear it.

keyTerms.meaning: That does not draw blood, a picture of נידוי

phrases.english: He sent him a message: If you do not come,
I will strike you with a thorn
that does not draw blood.
phrases.notes: He means he will put him in נידוי. It hurts, but no blood is spilled.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לָא אָתֵית מָחֵינָא לָךְ בְּסִילְוָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב נחמן's response to רב דימי's refusal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person must come to court when summoned and may not decide the case for himself.

steps.title: רב נחמן asks the witnesses what happened
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן asked the witnesses how the gift actually took place.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to the witnesses: 'How did the event happen?'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן looks into the facts by asking the witnesses exactly what happened when the gift was given. This sets up the answer that will decide the case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן wants to know the woman's state of mind when she gave the gift. Her exact words could show whether she gave it because she feared death.

phrases.english: He said to the witnesses:
How did the event happen?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After summoning רב דימי, רב נחמן checks the facts.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the woman said and how she acted when she gave the gift.

steps.title: The witnesses report her words: 'This woman is dying!'
steps.stepSummary: The witnesses said that at the time of the gift, she cried out, 'Woe, this woman is dying!'
steps.simpleTranslation: They told him that she said: 'Woe, this woman is dying!'
steps.whatsHappening: The witnesses answer רב נחמן's question by telling him exactly what she said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By 'this woman' she meant herself. Her words show clearly that she gave the gift because she thought she was about to die.

phrases.english: They said to him: This is what she said:
Woe, that this woman is dying!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב נחמן's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She openly said she was dying when she gave the gift.

steps.title: Ruling: a gift given because of expected death can be retracted
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן ruled that this was a gift given because she expected to die, and such a gift can be retracted.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: 'If so, she was giving directions because of death, and one who gives directions because of death can retract.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן decides the case for the woman: she may take back her gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב דימי relied on the leftover portion and the קנין. רב נחמן rules that because she openly said she was dying, the gift was clearly tied to her death. Since she did not die, she can take it back.

keyTerms.meaning: One who gives instructions about his property because he expects to die

steps.whatToRemember: When a person clearly says he is giving a gift because he is dying, he can take it back if he recovers. This holds here even though part of the property was left over and a קנין was made.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the leftover portion or the קנין won the case. Her own words about dying are what decided it.

phrases.english: He said to them: If so,
she was one who gives directions because of death,
and one who gives directions because of death can retract.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן הֲוָה מְצַוֶּה מֵחֲמַת מִיתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the law to the facts the witnesses reported.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A gift given in open expectation of death can be retracted on recovery, even when part of the property was left over and a קנין was made.

steps.title: A partial gift of a שכיב מרע is like both kinds of gift
steps.stepSummary: A ruling is quoted in the name of רב נחמן: when a שכיב מרע gives away only part of his property, the gift is like a healthy person's gift in one way and like a שכיב מרע's gift in another.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated about a gift of a שכיב מרע that covers only part of his property: The rabbis said before רבא, in the name of מר זוטרא son of רב נחמן, who said it in the name of רב נחמן: It is like the gift of a healthy person, and it is like the gift of a שכיב מרע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It brings a two-sided rule for a deathbed gift of only part of a person's property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of gift: a healthy person's gift, which needs a קנין and is final, and a שכיב מרע's gift, which needs no קנין and can be retracted. A partial gift by a שכיב מרע is a mixture of the two. The next step explains which feature comes from each side.

keyTerms.meaning: A person on his deathbed, seriously ill
The gift of a healthy person

phrases.english: It was stated:
About a gift of a person on his deathbed of only part of his property:
The rabbis said it before Rava

phrases.aramaic: מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּמָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
phrases.english: in the name of Mar Zutra, son of Rav Nachman,
who said it in the name of Rav Nachman:
It is like the gift of a healthy person,
and it is like the gift of a person on his deathbed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching after the story ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A partial gift of a שכיב מרע has features of both a healthy person's gift and a שכיב מרע's gift.

steps.title: Which feature comes from each kind of gift
steps.stepSummary: Like a healthy person's gift, it cannot be retracted if he recovers. Like a שכיב מרע's gift, it does not need a קנין.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like the gift of a healthy person: if he recovers, he cannot retract. And it is like the gift of a שכיב מרע: it does not need a קנין.
steps.whatsHappening: The ruling repeats both halves and explains what each comparison means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because he kept some property for himself, he was not giving everything away in fear of death, so the gift stays final if he recovers. Still, as a שכיב מרע, his spoken words alone transfer the gift without any formal קנין.

keyTerms.meaning: He stood up, meaning he recovered

steps.whatToRemember: This is the version the רבנן quoted in רב נחמן's name. רבא rejects it in the next step, and the הלכה in step 22 rules that a partial gift of a שכיב מרע does need a קנין.

phrases.english: It is like the gift of a healthy person:
if he recovers, he cannot retract,
and it is like the gift of a person on his deathbed:
it does not require an act of acquisition.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי הִיא כְּמַתְּנַת בָּרִיא שֶׁאִם עָמַד אֵינוֹ חוֹזֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two halves of the rule stated in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A partial deathbed gift cannot be retracted on recovery, yet it takes effect without a קנין.

steps.title: רבא rejects the quote attributed to רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the version of רב נחמן's ruling quoted in steps 8-9 is a false attribution.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to them: Didn't I tell you not to hang empty pitchers on רב נחמן?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects the version of רב נחמן's ruling we just heard. He is setting up his own correct version in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quote in steps 8-9 said a partial gift by a שכיב מרע does not need a קנין. רבא says רב נחמן never said that. 'Empty pitchers' is his picture for empty, made-up statements pinned on a great scholar.

keyTerms.meaning: empty pitchers; a picture for false statements

phrases.english: Rava said to them:
Did I not tell you:

phrases.aramaic: לָא תִּיתְלוֹ בּוּקֵי סְרִיקֵי בְּרַב נַחְמָן?
phrases.english: Do not hang empty pitchers on Rav Nachman?
phrases.notes: He means: don't pin made-up rulings on רב נחמן.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו אָמֵינָא לְכוּ: לָא תִּיתְלוֹ בּוּקֵי סְרִיקֵי בְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the attribution given in steps 8-9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole quoted version of רב נחמן's ruling
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It was wrongly attributed to רב נחמן.

steps.title: The correct version: a partial gift needs a קנין
steps.stepSummary: According to רבא, רב נחמן ruled that a שכיב מרע's partial gift is like a healthy person's gift and needs a קנין.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רב נחמן really said: it is like the gift of a healthy person, and it needs a קנין.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the true version of רב נחמן's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier version, a partial gift was like a שכיב מרע's gift in one way, because it needed no קנין. רבא's version removes that. The gift is fully like a healthy person's gift, so without a קנין it does not take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: the gift of a healthy person

steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes the position that the rest of the sugya tests and defends.

phrases.english: This is what Rav Nachman said:
It is like the gift of a healthy person,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the gift of a שכיב מרע who gave away only part of his property.

phrases.english: and it requires a kinyan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the corrected ruling after the rejection.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A partial gift by a שכיב מרע is like a healthy person's gift and needs a קנין.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה about leaving over land
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב נחמן from the משנה: if he left over some land, his gift stands. This seems to mean even without a קנין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא challenged רב נחמן: The משנה says if he left over any land, his gift stands. Isn't that talking about a case with no קנין?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא questions the ruling that a partial gift needs a קנין, using a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a sick man who kept some land for himself has a valid gift. If that is true even without a קנין, it contradicts the rule that a partial gift needs a קנין.

keyTerms.meaning: he left over, kept for himself

phrases.english: Rava challenged Rav Nachman:
If he left over any amount of land,
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה earlier in the פרק about a sick person's gift.

phrases.english: his gift stands.
What, is it not where they did not make a kinyan from him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a partial gift needs a קנין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה seems to validate a partial gift even without a קנין.

steps.title: The משנה is talking about a case with a קנין
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the משנה is talking about a case where a קנין was made.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the משנה is talking about a case where they made a קנין from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge is answered by reading the משנה as a case with a קנין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a קנין was made, it makes sense that the partial gift stands. So the משנה fits the rule that a partial gift needs a קנין.

keyTerms.meaning: they made a קנין from him

phrases.english: No, it is where they did make a kinyan from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is talking about a case with no קנין.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is talking about a case with a קנין, so it fits רב נחמן.

steps.title: Challenge from the second half of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה has a קנין, why does its last part say that when no land was left over, the gift does not stand?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the last part: if he did not leave over any land, his gift does not stand. If there was a קנין, why doesn't it stand?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on the answer using the סיפא, the last part of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the whole משנה is talking about a case with a קנין, then even a gift of everything should stand. A gift with a קנין is normally final. Yet the סיפא says it does not stand.

phrases.english: If so, say the last part:
If he did not leave over any amount of land,
his gift does not stand.
But if they made a kinyan from him,
why does his gift not stand?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the משנה is talking about a case with a קנין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A gift made with a קנין should not be cancelled, yet the סיפא cancels it.

steps.title: שמואל: a gift of everything can be retracted even with a קנין
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן quotes שמואל: a שכיב מרע who gave away everything can take it back if he recovers, even after a קנין, because clearly he gave only because he expected to die.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: שמואל said this: a שכיב מרע who wrote all his property to others can take it back if he recovers, even though a קנין was made. It is clear he gave only because he thought he was dying.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defends his reading with a rule of שמואל. This explains why the סיפא's gift fails even with a קנין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Giving away everything shows the gift was only because of expected death. So the gift falls away when he recovers, and the קנין does not change that. The whole משנה can therefore be talking about a case with a קנין.

keyTerms.meaning: a seriously ill person, on his deathbed
if he recovers, he takes it back
giving instructions because he expects to die

steps.whatToRemember: A קנין does not keep a gift of everything in place. If he recovers, he can retract, because it was clearly given only out of expected death.

phrases.english: He said to him: This is what Shmuel said:
A person on his deathbed who wrote
all his property to others,
even though they made a kinyan from him,
if he got up, he takes it back;
phrases.notes: 'Got up' means he recovered from his illness.

phrases.english: since it is known that he was not giving instructions
except because of death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Bringing a supporting rule from another אמורא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A gift with a קנין can never be retracted.
steps.terutzMaskana: A gift of everything is clearly given because of expected death, so it can be retracted on recovery even with a קנין.

steps.title: Challenge from the story of the mother of בני רוכל
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא challenges רבא: a sick woman gave away only her brooch, with no קנין mentioned, and her words were upheld after she died.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא challenged רבא: The mother of בני רוכל was sick and said, 'Give my brooch to my daughter.' It was worth twelve מנה. She died, and they upheld her words.
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge is raised against רבא's version, that a partial gift needs a קנין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The brooch was only part of her property, and no קנין was done. Yet the gift was upheld. This seems to show a partial gift works without a קנין.

keyTerms.meaning: a large coin, worth a hundred זוז

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiya challenged Rava:
There was an incident with the mother of the sons of Rokhel
who was sick, and she said:
"Let my brooch be given to my daughter"
and it was worth twelve maneh,
and she died, and they upheld her words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge against רבא's version in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's version: a partial gift needs a קנין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A partial gift with no קנין was upheld in a real case.

steps.title: That woman was giving because she expected to die
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the woman in the story was giving because she expected to die. That kind of gift works without a קנין.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, she was a person giving instructions because of death.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge by saying the story is a different kind of case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His rule about needing a קנין is for a sick person's ordinary partial gift. The woman in the story was clearly giving because she expected to die. That kind of gift works without a קנין once the giver dies, which is why her gift was upheld.
steps.confusionAlert: The woman gave only part of her property, yet she counts as giving because of death. Expecting death is what matters here, not whether she gave away everything.
steps.whatToRemember: A partial gift by a sick person needs a קנין, unless it is clearly given because the person expects to die. Then it works without a קנין.

phrases.english: There, it is one who gives instructions because of death.
phrases.notes: רבא is the one answering here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The story shows any partial gift works without a קנין.
steps.terutzMaskana: The story was a gift given because of expected death, which is a separate case that needs no קנין.

steps.title: רבינא challenges רבא from the case of the גט and the מנה
steps.stepSummary: רבינא brings a משנה: a גט or a שטר שחרור is not delivered after the man dies, but 'give a מנה to so-and-so' is paid after his death.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא challenged רבא: If someone says 'Give this גט to my wife and this שטר שחרור to my slave' and then dies, they do not give them after his death. If he says 'Give a מנה to so-and-so' and dies, they do give it after his death.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא quotes a משנה that seems to show a dying man's small gift working without any קנין. He uses it to challenge רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מנה is only a small part of his property, so it is a partial gift (מקצת). רבא held that a partial gift needs a קנין unless the man is a מצוה מחמת מיתה. Here the money is paid with no קנין mentioned, so the משנה seems to go against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: A document that frees a slave
A sum of money (one hundred זוז)

phrases.english: Ravina challenged Rava:
One who says: "Give this get to my wife,
and this freedom document to my slave,"
and he died: they should not give them after his death.
"Give a maneh to so-and-so,"
and he died: they do give it after his death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to רבא, after רב משרשיא's challenge was answered in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's view that a partial gift of a שכיב מרע needs a קנין unless he gives because he expects to die.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה has a partial gift (a מנה) paid after death with no קנין and no mention of the man expecting to die.

steps.title: Proving that the משנה has no קנין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know no קנין was made, and answers that the מנה case is placed next to the גט, which cannot work through a קנין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that no קנין was made with him? It is like the גט. Just as a גט is not something a קנין works for, so too this case is one where no קנין was made.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבינא's challenge. It shows that the משנה really is talking about a gift with no קנין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might answer that the משנה's gift had a קנין. The גמרא points out that the money case is placed right next to the גט. A גט does not work through a קנין, so the money case must also be without one. That makes the challenge to רבא stronger.

They made a קנין with him (to lock in the gift)

phrases.english: And how do we know that no kinyan was made with him?
It is like the get:
just as a get is not something a kinyan works for,

phrases.aramaic: אַף הַאי נָמֵי דְּלָא קְנוֹ מִינֵּיהּ!
phrases.english: so too this case is one where no kinyan was made with him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the קשיא of step 18 by blocking the answer that the משנה had a קנין.
steps.raayaObject: That the מנה gift in the משנה was made without a קנין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה places the מנה case next to the get, which does not work through a קנין.

steps.title: רבא answers: that man was also giving because he expected to die
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the משנה is talking about a מצוה מחמת מיתה, so no קנין is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, it is talking about someone giving instructions because he expects to die.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge the same way he answered in step 17. The man in the משנה was giving because he expected to die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא agrees there was no קנין. He says the man is a מצוה מחמת מיתה, and that kind of gift works without a קנין even when it is only part of his property. So the משנה fits his view.

keyTerms.meaning: One who gives instructions because he expects to die

phrases.english: There too,
it is about someone giving instructions because he expects to die.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 18-19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the משנה is a מצוה מחמת מיתה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה looked like an ordinary partial gift that worked without a קנין.
steps.terutzMaskana: The man gave because he expected to die, and such a gift needs no קנין.

steps.title: רב הונא says giving because of death usually needs a קנין
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says a מצוה מחמת מיתה normally needs a קנין. The sources that don't require one are talking about someone who gave away all his property.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא the son of רב יהושע said: Someone who gives instructions because he expects to die generally needs a קנין. When these sources teach that none is needed, they mean someone who divides all his property, because that was given the status of a מתנת שכיב מרע.
steps.whatsHappening: A different אמורא gives another way to explain the sources. It disagrees with רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, a מצוה מחמת מיתה is enough to skip the קנין. For רב הונא, the key factor is giving away everything, which is the full status of a מתנת שכיב מרע. In his view, the sources without a קנין are all cases of a man dividing his whole estate.

keyTerms.meaning: The gift of a dangerously sick person, which works without a קנין
They (the חכמים) gave it the status of

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Huna the son of Rav Yehoshua said:

phrases.aramaic: מְצַוֶּה מֵחֲמַת מִיתָה בְּעָלְמָא – בָּעֲיָא קִנְיָן,
phrases.english: someone giving instructions because he expects to die generally needs a kinyan,
and when these sources teach otherwise,
phrases.notes: He means the sources quoted above, where the gift worked with no קנין.

phrases.english: they mean someone who divides all his property,
because that was given the status of a gift of a shechiv mera.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different way to explain the sources than רבא's answers in steps 17 and 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מצוה מחמת מיתה needs a קנין unless he gives away all his property.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two terms. מצוה מחמת מיתה is about why he gives (he expects to die). מתנת שכיב מרע in the full sense here is about how much he gives (everything).

steps.title: The final הלכה on gifts of a dying person
steps.stepSummary: A partial gift of a שכיב מרע needs a קנין even if he dies. A מצוה מחמת מיתה needs no קנין, but only if he dies. If he recovers, he can take it back even after a קנין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה is: A שכיב מרע's gift of part of his property needs a קנין, even if he died. Someone giving instructions because he expects to die does not need a קנין, but only if he died. If he got better, he can take it back, even if a קנין was made with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the final הלכה. It follows רבא's distinction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three rules. (1) An ordinary partial gift of a sick man needs a קנין, and his death does not fix it. (2) A gift made because he expects to die works without a קנין once he dies. This follows רבא and goes against רב הונא in step 21. (3) If he recovers, the whole gift falls away, even with a קנין, because it was based on his expected death. This is what רב נחמן ruled in step 7, and it uses the same reasoning שמואל gave in step 15.

phrases.aramaic: וְהִלְכְתָא: מַתְּנַת שְׁכִיב מְרַע בְּמִקְצָת – בָּעֲיָא קִנְיָן,
phrases.english: And the halacha is: a shechiv mera's gift of part of his property needs a kinyan,
even though he died.

phrases.aramaic: מְצַוֶּה מֵחֲמַת מִיתָה לָא בָּעֲיָא קִנְיָן,
phrases.english: Someone giving instructions because he expects to die does not need a kinyan,
but only if he died;
if he recovered, he can take it back,
even though a kinyan was made with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the approaches in favor of רבא's distinction.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A partial gift by a שכיב מרע needs a קנין. A מצוה מחמת מיתה needs none if he dies, and is void if he recovers, even with a קנין.
steps.whatToRemember: Two questions decide the case: Did he give because he expected to die? Did he die? If he gave a regular partial gift, he needs a קנין. If he gave because he expected to die, no קנין is needed, but if he recovers, the gift falls away anyway.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical rule for a dying person's gifts, so it matters in real cases of wills and inheritance.
